anomalies.observed: Both sides of each isolated CAN transceiver are connected to the same GND net: U10 pins 4 (GND1) and 5 (GND2), and U11 pins 4 (GND1) and 5 (GND2).
anomalies.expected: To provide the specified CAN galvanic isolation, each transceiver's GND1 and GND2 must remain electrically separate; the isolation barrier must not be bypassed by a shared ground.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The shared ground bypasses the transceivers' isolation barriers, so the CAN interfaces do not provide galvanic isolation and may permit ground-loop or fault currents between the controller side and external CAN wiring.

parsed.summary: An anomaly is present: both isolated CAN transceivers have their GND1 and GND2 pins tied to the same GND net. This defeats the galvanic isolation specified for the CAN interfaces.
